images.caption:
The train north from Inverness through the Scottish Highlands consists of diesel railcars.  You have a choice of two destinations.  There is a junction, and the train splits.  One part (or one car) goes to Thurso, and the other to Wick.  I chose Thurso.  John o'Groats, nominally the northernmost point in mainland Britain, is a few miles away.

Old St. Peter's Kirk (church) was built around 1220 and closed in the 1830s.  The location is approximate.

images.filename: Northern Constabulary at Highland Games, Helmsdale Sutherland Scotland (6063996938).jpg
images.caption:
Sergeant Peter Allan, Brora, supervises Northern Constabulary Pipe Band as they tune up for Massed Bands.
The Annual Highland Games in Helmsdale is a big day in the local calendar, and this year the weather was kind. 

Northern Constabulary was, as always in attendance, especially for the parade from the village centre to the Games field at Couper Park - which entails regualting traffic on the main trunk road to allow the parade safe passage. Thereafter the local officers patrol the Games field and interact with the public in the best traditions of Scottish community policing.

images.filename: Italian Chapel - Lamb Holm - Orkney - kingsley - 29-JUN-09.JPG
images.caption: Front quarter profile of the Italian Chapel on the small isle called Lamb Holm.  This is located on the edge of Scapa Flow in the Orkney Islands (north of Great Britain).  The chapel was built by WWII Italian prisoners of war captured in North Africa and put to work on the Churchill Barriers in the Orkney Islands.  Using the limited materials they had leftover from the barrier project, the prisoners converted two nissin huts into this chapel.  Much of the artistic work was done by Domenico Chiocchetti who returned to finish his work after the war ended.
